title: Feasibility Of Sleep Treatment Education in Stroke Rehabilitation Settings
official: Feasibility Of Sleep Treatment Education in Stroke Rehabilitation Settings
summary:
Stroke is a leading cause of disability with over 1 million people in the UK living with the effects of stroke. Sleep is important for many aspects of daily life, but there is growing evidence that people sleep worse after a stroke, and this impacts negatively on rehabilitation outcomes and quality of life. Stroke survivors have highlighted to us that it is difficult to sleep in the hospital after a stroke, and they feel that sleep isn't perceived as high priority despite clear importance for next day function and healing.

This project will develop and test a sleep education package for clinical staff and stroke survivors in the rehabilitation hospital. Specifically, we aim to (1) develop a training programme for staff and a toolkit of resources about sleep for staff and stroke survivors, (2) assess acceptability and usability of the package, and, following modifications, (3) assess the feasibility of delivery of the sleep education package and collecting data about patient's sleep.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

Stroke survivors:

* Neurorehabilitation unit inpatient
* Clinical diagnosis of stroke
* Aged 18 years or over
* Willing and able to provide informed consent OR a positive opinion from a consultee is provided by a family member or carer (relative or friend) willing to provide personal consultee (PC) advice.

Staff:

* Current stroke rehabilitation unit staff member, providing care to stroke survivors
* Aged 18 years or over
* Able and willing to provide informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

* Staff may not participate if they are anticipated to be leaving the neurorehabilitation unit within 2 months of the delivery of the sleep education package
* Stroke survivors may not participate if they are anticipated to be discharged within 1 week of recruitment
